# The decoder benchmark: a small, fixed workload decoded in interleaved rounds on one
# runner, by examples/ab.rs (`ab run`), and its figures (bench/report.py).
#
# - A pull request: its head against its base (the merge base with master), both built
#   here and run as two arms of one harness (`mibz2` and `mibz2@base/ab`, the base's own
#   harness binary), so the builds run in the same process shape, their order alternating
#   round to round. The figures go to one comment on the pull request, edited in place.
#   Nothing from a pull request is recorded.
# - A push to master: the commit's mibz2 against the alternatives (pbz2, the lbzip2 CLI,
#   indexed_bzip2, fbz, the lbzip2 crate, libbzip2, libbz2-rs, bz2ngrs and bz2-ng's C),
#   and its inverse BWT against bz2ngrs's and libsais's, its result kept on the
#   bench-results branch (a data-only branch, never merged; nothing is committed to
#   master). The site's benchmark pages are built from it.
# - From the Actions tab: any ref, against the alternatives as on master, or against
#   `base` if given (as on a pull request). Its figures are the run's summary and
#   artifact, never recorded.
#
# The alternatives that are Rust crates with dependencies of their own (fbz, the lbzip2
# crate, libbz2-rs, bz2ngrs) are arms of bench/alternatives' build of the harness
# (`ARM@alts/ab`); indexed_bzip2 runs through Python (bench/ib.py, AB_PYTHON), and bz2-ng's
# C as its own `bzip2 -dc`, built here at a pinned commit (AB_BZ2NG). Single-threaded
# decoders (libbzip2, libbz2-rs, bz2ngrs, bz2ng) run at 1 thread only (examples/ab.rs:
# `parallel`).
#
# The workload: the crate's corpora (`ab gen`, tests/common/mod.rs) at a small scale, and
# 12 MB of the Wikidata dump's own bzip2 blocks (bench/wikidata.json: byte-range windows
# of a dated dump, each window's SHA-256 and the corpus's pinned). At 1 thread, at 2 (one
# CPU on each of 2 cores, `--spread`: the runners' 4 CPUs are 2 cores) and at the runner's
# CPUs, ROUNDS rounds. The 2-thread runs (about 40 s of the run) give CPU amplification
# free of SMT: the report's resources table and its assessment (bench/report.py).
#
# The stages (bench/stages.py): each build's examples/phases.rs on the Wikidata blocks,
# pinned to one CPU, STAGE_ROUNDS rounds of each build once, each stage's fastest of
# STAGE_REPEATS passes of the file in decode order; a
# table of each stage's cycles a byte (head over base on a pull request), beside the
# decoder's figures, not part of them.
name: Benchmark

on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened, ready_for_review]
    paths:
      - "src/**"
      - "Cargo.toml"
      - "Cargo.lock"
      - "examples/ab.rs"
      - "examples/windows.rs"
      - "examples/phases.rs"
      - "tests/common/**" # (the corpora's recipe)
      - "bench/**"
      - ".github/workflows/bench.yml"
  push:
    branches: [master]
    paths:
      - "src/**"
      - "Cargo.toml"
      - "Cargo.lock"
      - "examples/ab.rs"
      - "examples/windows.rs"
      - "examples/phases.rs"
      - "tests/common/**"
      - "bench/**"
      - ".github/workflows/bench.yml"
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      base:
        description: "A commit to compare against, as on a pull request (empty: mibz2 against the alternatives, as on master)"
        required: false
      base_sample_ms:
        description: "The base arm's thread sampler interval (AB_SAMPLE_MS; 0: none). With base set to the head commit, this measures the sampler's own cost to the decode"
        required: false

# A push to a pull request cancels its run in progress; master's runs each make a record
concurrency:
  group: bench-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.sha }}-${{ inputs.base }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

permissions:
  contents: write # (master: the bench-results and bench-data branches)
  pull-requests: write # (the comment)

env:
  ROUNDS: 10
  SCALE: 4 # ab gen's: corpora of 8-20 MB of output each
  SETTLE: 0.25 # seconds the harness samples the other processes' load before each run
  STAGE_ROUNDS: 5 # bench/stages.py's rounds (each 13-17 s on the runners seen)
  STAGE_REPEATS: 2 # phases' passes a run, each a decode of the file (each stage's fastest kept)
  KERNEL_PASSES: 10 # bench/alternatives' kernels: passes of both inverse BWTs over the Wikidata blocks (about 3 s each)
  RUN_URL: ${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: never

jobs:
  bench:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 60
    steps:
      # A pull request's head commit itself, not GitHub's merge of it into the base
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Arms
        env:
          PR_HEAD: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          PR_BASE: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          INPUT_BASE: ${{ inputs.base }}
        run: |
          head=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
          case "$GITHUB_EVENT_NAME" in
            pull_request) mode=pr; base=$(git merge-base "$PR_BASE" "$PR_HEAD") ;;
            push) mode=master; base= ;;
            *) if [ -n "$INPUT_BASE" ]; then mode=pr; base=$(git rev-parse "$INPUT_BASE^{commit}"); else mode=dispatch; base=; fi ;;
          esac
          if [ "$mode" = pr ]; then
            arms="mibz2,mibz2@base/ab"
          else
            arms="mibz2,pbz2,lbzip2,indexed_bzip2,fbz@alts/ab,lbzip2-rs@alts/ab,libbzip2,libbz2-rs@alts/ab,bz2ngrs@alts/ab,bz2ng"
          fi
          {
            echo "MODE=$mode"; echo "HEAD_SHA=$head"; echo "BASE_SHA=$base"; echo "ARMS=$arms"
            echo "HEAD_DATE=$(git show -s --format=%cI "$head")"
          } >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          echo "mode $mode, head $head, base ${base:-none}, arms $arms"

      - name: Comment (pending)
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
        continue-on-error: true # (a fork's pull request has a read-only token)
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: python3 bench/comment.py pending ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }} "$HEAD_SHA"

      # lbzip2: an arm, and examples/windows.rs's check of the Wikidata blocks
      - name: lbzip2
        run: sudo apt-get install -y -qq lbzip2 > /dev/null && lbzip2 --version | head -1

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2

      # The release profile (Cargo.toml's: fat LTO, one codegen unit), as published
      - name: Build the head
        run: |
          cargo build --release --example ab --example windows --example phases
          mkdir -p bin && cp target/release/examples/ab bin/ab && cp target/release/examples/phases bin/phases

      # The alternatives (master and the Actions tab only): bench/alternatives' build of the
      # harness, and indexed_bzip2 in a virtualenv of its own
      - name: Build the alternatives
        if: env.MODE != 'pr'
        run: |
          # libsais 2.12.1 at a pinned commit, single-threaded, for the kernels binary's libsais
          # kernel (bench/libsais.sh: its source checked by SHA-256)
          # (two steps, so a failed build fails the step: `export` would hide its status)
          LIBSAIS_DIR=$(bash bench/libsais.sh "$RUNNER_TEMP/libsais")
          export LIBSAIS_DIR
          CARGO_TARGET_DIR="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/target/alts" cargo build --release --locked --manifest-path bench/alternatives/Cargo.toml
          mkdir -p alts && cp target/alts/release/ab target/alts/release/kernels alts/
          # bz2-ng's C at a pinned commit, its CLI (CMake's Release build, as its README builds it)
          ng=517948ed836d4c52d68d8e633887aaa21c17ba27
          git init -q "$RUNNER_TEMP/bz2-ng" && git -C "$RUNNER_TEMP/bz2-ng" fetch -q --depth 1 https://github.com/tfenne/bz2-ng "$ng"
          git -C "$RUNNER_TEMP/bz2-ng" checkout -q FETCH_HEAD
          cmake -S "$RUNNER_TEMP/bz2-ng/c" -B "$RUNNER_TEMP/bz2-ng/build" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DBZ2NG_BUILD_SHARED=OFF \
            -DBZ2NG_BUILD_TESTS=OFF -DBZ2NG_BUILD_BENCH=OFF -DBZ2NG_BUILD_FUZZ=OFF > /dev/null
          cmake --build "$RUNNER_TEMP/bz2-ng/build" -j "$(nproc)" --target bzip2 > /dev/null
          echo "AB_BZ2NG=$RUNNER_TEMP/bz2-ng/build/bzip2" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          python3 -m venv "$RUNNER_TEMP/ib" && "$RUNNER_TEMP/ib/bin/pip" install -q indexed_bzip2==1.7.0
          echo "AB_PYTHON=$RUNNER_TEMP/ib/bin/python" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      - name: Build the base
        if: env.MODE == 'pr'
        env:
          BASE_SAMPLE_MS: ${{ inputs.base_sample_ms }}
        run: |
          git worktree add --detach .base-src "$BASE_SHA"
          test -f .base-src/examples/ab.rs || { echo "::error::the base $BASE_SHA has no examples/ab.rs"; exit 1; }
          # (and its examples/phases.rs, for the stage table, where it has one)
          phases=$(test -f .base-src/examples/phases.rs && echo "--example phases" || true)
          (cd .base-src && CARGO_TARGET_DIR="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/target" cargo build --release --example ab $phases)
          mkdir -p base && cp target/release/examples/ab base/ab
          if [ -n "$phases" ]; then cp target/release/examples/phases base/phases; fi
          # (the Actions tab only: the base arm with its own sampler interval, AB_SAMPLE_MS)
          if [ -n "$BASE_SAMPLE_MS" ]; then
            mv base/ab base/ab-bin
            printf '#!/bin/sh\nAB_SAMPLE_MS=%s exec "%s" "$@"\n' "$BASE_SAMPLE_MS" "$PWD/base/ab-bin" > base/ab
            chmod +x base/ab
            echo "base arm: AB_SAMPLE_MS=$BASE_SAMPLE_MS"
          fi

      - name: Corpora
        run: bin/ab gen corpora "$SCALE"

      # Wikimedia serves a dated dump for about six weeks: the windows are kept on the
      # bench-data branch once a master run has read them, and read from there first
      - name: Wikidata windows (cache)
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: windows
          key: bench-wikidata-${{ hashFiles('bench/wikidata.json') }}

      - name: Wikidata windows
        run: |
          dir=$(python3 -c 'import json; print(json.load(open("bench/wikidata.json"))["windows_dir"])')
          if [ "$(ls "$dir"/*.bin 2>/dev/null | wc -l)" = 0 ] && git fetch -q origin bench-data:refs/remotes/origin/bench-data 2>/dev/null; then
            git archive origin/bench-data "$dir" | tar -x || true
          fi
          source=$(python3 bench/wikidata.py fetch bench/wikidata.json "$dir")
          echo "WINDOWS_SOURCE=$source" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          echo "WINDOWS_DIR=$dir" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          python3 bench/wikidata.py build bench/wikidata.json "$dir" target/release/examples/windows corpora/wikidata.bz2
          ls -l corpora

      # The runner as the runs see it (cores, quota, the run-queue counter's check)
      - name: Environment
        run: bin/ab env | tee env.json

      - name: Run
        run: |
          threads=$([ "$(nproc)" -gt 2 ] && echo "1,2,$(nproc)" || echo "1,$(nproc)")
          bin/ab run runs.jsonl --arms "$ARMS" --threads "$threads" --spread --rounds "$ROUNDS" --settle "$SETTLE" corpora/*.bz2

      # Each stage on its own, on one thread: a diagnostic beside the decoder's figures
      - name: Stages
        run: |
          if [ "$MODE" = pr ]; then
            arms="head=bin/phases"; [ -x base/phases ] && arms="base=base/phases $arms"
          else
            arms="mibz2=bin/phases"
          fi
          start=$SECONDS
          python3 bench/stages.py run stages.jsonl --rounds "$STAGE_ROUNDS" --repeats "$STAGE_REPEATS" corpora/wikidata.bz2 $arms
          echo "stages: $((SECONDS - start)) s"

      # The inverse BWT alone, mibz2's against bz2ngrs's phase by phase, on one CPU (master
      # and the Actions tab only: bench/alternatives' kernels binary)
      - name: Kernels
        if: env.MODE != 'pr'
        run: |
          start=$SECONDS
          taskset -c 1 alts/kernels corpora/wikidata.bz2 "$KERNEL_PASSES" kernels.jsonl
          echo "kernels: $((SECONDS - start)) s"

      # the report's stage table across builds whose phases report different stages
      - name: Report tests
        run: python3 bench/test_report.py

      - name: Figures
        run: |
          ref=$([ "$MODE" = pr ] && echo "mibz2@base/ab" || echo mibz2)
          { echo "## ab summary (reference: $ref)"; bin/ab summary runs.jsonl --ref "$ref"; } > ab-summary.md
          python3 bench/report.py summary runs.jsonl --corpora corpora --mode "$MODE" --head "$HEAD_SHA" \
            ${BASE_SHA:+--base "$BASE_SHA"} --date "$HEAD_DATE" --run "$RUN_URL" --stages stages.jsonl --env env.json --kernels kernels.jsonl \
            --out result.json --md comment.md
          cat comment.md ab-summary.md >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          # (the resources section in the log too, where a dispatched run's figures can be read)
          sed -n '/^### Resources/,/^<\/details>/p' comment.md

      - name: Comment
        if: "!cancelled() && github.event_name == 'pull_request'"
        continue-on-error: true
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if [ -f comment.md ]; then
            python3 bench/comment.py final ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }} comment.md
          else
            python3 bench/comment.py failed ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }} "$HEAD_SHA"
          fi

      - name: Results
        if: "!cancelled()"
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: bench-${{ env.MODE }}-${{ env.HEAD_SHA }}
          path: |
            runs.jsonl
            env.json
            stages.jsonl
            kernels.jsonl
            result.json
            comment.md
            ab-summary.md
          if-no-files-found: ignore

      # master only: the commit's result appended to the bench-results branch, and the
      # Wikidata windows kept on the bench-data branch if they were read from Wikimedia
      - name: Record
        if: success() && github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/master'
        run: |
          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git config user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          # (a data-only branch, checked out beside the code: its last commit, or a new one)
          open_branch() {
            if git fetch -q origin "$1:refs/remotes/origin/$1" 2>/dev/null; then
              git worktree add -q --detach "$2" "origin/$1"
            else
              git worktree add -q --orphan -b "$1" "$2"
            fi
          }
          push_branch() {
            for try in 1 2 3; do
              git -C "$2" push -q origin "HEAD:$1" && return 0
              git -C "$2" fetch -q origin "$1" && git -C "$2" rebase -q FETCH_HEAD
            done
            return 1
          }
          open_branch bench-results .store
          python3 bench/report.py record .store result.json runs.jsonl
          git -C .store add -A
          git -C .store commit -qm "record bench: ${HEAD_SHA::7}, bench $(python3 -c 'import json; print(json.load(open("result.json"))["bench"])')"
          push_branch bench-results .store
          if [ "$WINDOWS_SOURCE" != kept ] || ! git cat-file -e "origin/bench-data:$WINDOWS_DIR" 2>/dev/null; then
            open_branch bench-data .data
            mkdir -p ".data/$WINDOWS_DIR" && cp "$WINDOWS_DIR"/*.bin ".data/$WINDOWS_DIR/" && cp bench/wikidata.json ".data/$WINDOWS_DIR/"
            python3 bench/wikidata.py readme bench/wikidata.json > .data/README.md
            git -C .data add -A
            if git -C .data diff --cached --quiet; then
              echo "bench-data already holds $WINDOWS_DIR"
            else
              git -C .data commit -qm "bench data: $WINDOWS_DIR"
              push_branch bench-data .data
            fi
          fi

What the model assumes
  • Linear in bytes: the scanner's time in the dump's bz2 bytes, the workers' in its output bytes.
  • The sample stands for the dump: 12 windows of 1 MiB at (2i + 1)/24 of the dump, 431 of its own blocks; their mix of entities and their ratio, 17.69× (the windows' 95% interval ±14.0%), stand for the whole dump's. Another sample of the same dump (wikidata-pq's bench/full, 24 windows of 25 MB) measured 18.68×; wikidata-pq's CI slice, lines recompressed, is 13.69×.
  • The wall at N threads is the larger of the scanner's time and the workers' time over N (the scanner is one thread; the workers run blocks in parallel), times the sample's own wall over that bound: its overlap and fill taken to grow with the work, which errs long. Read as a fixed cost instead, the same gap gives the third row.
  • The machine is this runner, reading the dump from page cache: no download, no disk, no other work. The output is hashed by the reading thread and discarded.
  • The uncertainty is the rounds' spread, with the sample ratio's added in quadrature to the part that scales with the output; not the runner's: another CPU model gives other figures.
